images.caption: Figure 3:UE5 paired training data.(a) Each clip is captured twice in Unreal Engine 5 under the same camera and frame index: once as a low-poly structure render (BBox) that preserves scene layout and motion, and once as the high-fidelity RGB frame. (b) For every 81-frame clip, frame-aligned CSV records of camera pose, actions, visible objects, events, and environment are turned into a prompt: visible object IDs are looked up in a description table, spatial and temporal cues are composed, and a template produces the clip prompt.

Figure 4:Dynamic captions follow the engine state.Top: low-poly proxy frames of one CitySample driving clip; numbered markers are the visible objects that the engine reports for this frame, each linked by its instance ID to a semantic description. Below: the caption that the rule-based template produces for the same frame, without any vision-language model. Orange text comes from object states and events, and blue text from object positions and distances. As the car moves, parked vehicles leave the description, pedestrians change from standing to approaching, and newly visible objects are announced under “Changes”.

Figure 7:Re-rendering over 40-second held-out rollouts.For each game, the upper row is the low-poly proxy from the engine and the lower row is the frame generated by the distilled causal model at the same time step. The generated frames follow the proxy layout, camera, and object motion throughout the rollout, while the model fills in materials, vegetation, lighting, smoke, and muzzle effects.

Figure 8:Game modes written with the coding agent, rendered in real time.Top: in the third-person shooter, the agent adds health and ammunition control, shield durability, a faster shotgun, a game-over condition, and simple sound effects. Middle: in the driving game, the agent implements a time trial with route checkpoints and collision penalties. Bottom: the same driving game turned into a pursuit mode, in which the player must intercept a target vehicle and stay close to it for five seconds. The engine evaluates every rule; the video model renders each frame from the engine output.
